- If sentiment is negative and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent price spike is followed by forecast overshoot, cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect; apply downward bias of 2–5% in early forecast days.  
- If forecast mean is > true mean by >3%, check for sentiment lag: if sentiment is positive but price is falling, reduce forecast by 3–5% to align with sentiment drift.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 80), reduce forecast slope to match downward trend.  
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility spikes (e.g., 2+ consecutive high sentiment values), forecast should be capped at 10% below peak to avoid overestimating volatility.
